title: Settlement Timing Rule — Start of the RideLink Settlement Clock
content:
The lateness of a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation trip settlement is measured from the start of the settlement clock, the date the records show the trip could first be settled.

**Rule.** The settlement clock starts on a date set by the records that show when the trip could first be settled: when the member's paid outpatient hospital claim with the latest service date was booked after the return leg's appointment date, the clock starts on that claim's booked date; when no such claim was booked after the return leg's appointment date but the return leg was registered after the outbound leg's appointment date, because the stay was extended while the member was away, the clock starts on the return leg's registration date; otherwise the clock starts on the return leg's appointment date.

The claim looked at is one claim: among the member's claims under their Medicaid Managed Care Membership in the outpatient hospital category and adjudicated as paid, the one with the latest service date; what matters is the date that claim was booked. The return leg and outbound leg are the member's latest registered legs of each kind; the return leg's registration date is the date it was booked.

## Branches, taken in order

| Test | If it holds, the clock starts on |
|---|---|
| The latest-service paid outpatient hospital claim was booked after the return appointment date | That claim's booked date |
| Otherwise: the return leg was registered after the outbound appointment date | The return leg's registration date |
| Otherwise | The return leg's appointment date |

## Cases

*Hypothetical trip:* outbound appointment 10 March, return appointment 20 March.

- The latest-service paid outpatient hospital claim was booked on 2 April: the clock starts on 2 April.
- That claim was booked on 18 March, and the return leg was registered on 15 March: the claim test fails; the return leg was registered after 10 March, so the clock starts on 15 March.
- That claim was booked on 18 March, and the return leg was registered on 1 March: the clock starts on 20 March.
- No such claim exists and the return leg was registered on 1 March: the clock starts on 20 March.
